Optimal Classification scaling

Source: R/svt.R
optcls.Rd

Nonparametric ideal points from binary votes in the spirit of Poole (2000): each vote's cutting direction is the unit-length difference of the mean positions of its yea and nay voters, each legislator moves to the mean of the directions of the sides taken, for maxit sweeps from each of nstart random starts; the start with the fewest classification errors is kept. A vote is split at the point of its direction that misclassifies fewest of its voters, either side voting yea, so no vote has more errors than voting with the majority.

Usage

optcls(votes, ndim = 1, maxit = 500, nstart = 10, seed = 42)

Arguments

votes

A legislator-by-vote matrix: 1 yea, 0 nay, NA absent.

ndim

The number of dimensions; ndim times the points scaled must be at most 67108864 (2^26).

maxit

The sweeps per start.

nstart

The random starts.

seed

The seed of the starts, as set.seed() takes it.

Value

A list of class optcls: ideal, normals (votes by dimensions), pre (the proportional reduction in error), errors, null (the errors of voting with the majority on every vote) and ndim.

References

Poole, K. T. (2000). Nonparametric unfolding of binary choice data. Political Analysis, 8(3), 211-237. doi:10.1093/oxfordjournals.pan.a029814

See also

Other scaling: amscal(), anchv(), anomin(), bamscl(), bbscal(), bmdsf(), bunfld(), cjrirt(), cmdsf(), cutlns(), dblctr(), dwnom(), dynirt(), indscl(), ipsrec(), irtem(), irtlik(), irtpst(), mdsfit(), mlsmu(), nmdsf(), nombt(), nomll(), nompr(), nomutl(), nrmvec(), ordirt(), ordocl(), procrs(), scboot(), smacf(), smunf(), unfstr(), votagr(), wrdfsh()

Examples

# 20 simulated legislators, 30 votes cut along one dimension
set.seed(1)
x <- sort(rnorm(20))
v <- outer(x, rnorm(30), ">") * 1
optcls(v, maxit = 20, nstart = 2)$pre
#> [1] 1
